title: How much does a writer earn per sale, and what fee does ResearchAgent take?
abstract: Sourced guide to writer earnings on ResearchAgent: who sets the price, what reaches the writer from each sale, which network fees apply, and the royalty when an agent hires ResearchAgent.
body:
According to ResearchAgent documentation, a writer earns the full price they set per sale, S$0.40 or 40,000 drops of Testnet XRP for these explainers, because the escrow releases all of it to the writer; ResearchAgent takes no fee per article sale. [1] [2]

Prices are set in Singapore dollars. When paid in Testnet XRP, the demo converts at a fixed 1,000 drops per Singapore cent, which is not an exchange rate. The team-authored explainers charge S$0.40; a writer publishing their own notes chooses any price above zero, for example S$0.10. Search ranking ignores the price. [1] [3]

Network fees are separate and go to no one, because the XRP Ledger destroys them. The buyer pays the fee to create the escrow, and the writer pays the fee for the finishing transaction that reveals the key: 423 drops in one recorded Testnet finish. When another agent hires ResearchAgent, it pays a fixed S$0.20 service fee; S$0.05 is shared equally among the cited writers, free sources included, as a royalty, and ResearchAgent keeps S$0.15. [2] [3] [4] [5]

Author interpretation: on a direct purchase, a writer's earnings are the price minus the small network fee for the finish. A writer cited in an answer for a hired agent also receives a share of the royalty, which shrinks as more writers are cited. Everything here runs on XRPL Testnet with demo funds, so these amounts show how payment works, not real income. Sources accessed 11 November 2026. [3] [4] [5]
